message.content:
Based on my search, I can provide you with comprehensive information about what opioids are derived from.

## Primary Source: The Opium Poppy Plant

The vast majority of opioids trace their origins to the **opium poppy plant (*Papaver somniferum*)**. This plant produces a resinous latex called **opium**, which contains natural opioid alkaloids including:

- **Morphine** – the most abundant and medically significant natural opioid
- **Codeine** – another major natural opioid used for pain relief and cough suppression
- **Thebaine** – a stimulant alkaloid that serves as a critical precursor for many semi-synthetic opioids

## Three Categories of Opioid Origins

### 1. Natural Opioids (Opiates)
These are compounds found directly in opium:
- Morphine
- Codeine
- Thebaine

### 2. Semi-Synthetic Opioids
These are chemically modified versions of natural opium alkaloids:
- **Heroin** (diacetylmorphine) – derived from morphine
- **Oxycodone** – synthesized from thebaine
- **Hydrocodone** – derived from codeine or thebaine
- **Hydromorphone** – derived from morphine
- **Buprenorphine** – derived from thebaine
- **Naloxone** – synthesized from thebaine

### 3. Fully Synthetic Opioids
These are manufactured in laboratories without using natural opium as a starting material, though they are designed to mimic the effects of natural opioids:
- **Fentanyl**
- **Methadone**
- **Meperidine (Demerol)**
- **Tramadol**

## How Natural Opioids Are Obtained

The opium alkaloids are found in the **latex** (a milky white fluid) that exudes from the seed pods of the opium poppy when cut. This latex dries to become raw opium. Specialized poppy cultivars have also been bred to produce higher concentrations of specific alkaloids—for example, "Norman" and "Penelope" strains are bred for high thebaine and low morphine content.

## Other Natural Sources

Research has also identified opioid-like compounds in other organisms:
- **Endogenous opioids** – peptides naturally produced in the human body (endorphins, enkephalins)
- **Amphibian opioid peptides** – such as dermorphins and deltorphins found in the skin of certain frogs
- **Exorphins** – opioid peptides derived from exogenous proteins such as milk (β-casomorphins) and wheat gluten

2. https://odfree.org/history-of-opioids/
3. https://www.getsmartaboutdrugs.gov/sites/getsmartaboutdrugs.com/files/publications/Drugs%20of%20Abuse%202020-Web%20Version-508%20compliant-4-24-20.pdf
4. https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/oxymorphone
5. https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/nursing-and-health-professions/papaver-somniferum
